newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end up 0.47 pct ahead of futures expir.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end up 0.47 pct ahead of futures expir.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed up 0.47 percent in heavy trade dominated by major players speculating ahead of Monday's options settlements, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49-most-traded shares ended up 321 points at 67,981 points. Turnover was 570 million reais ($556.2 million).
Bellwether Telebras preferred shares ended up 0.49 percent at 82.70 reais.
Although volatility ahead of the futures expiry has been increasing throughout the week, analysts noted it has been lower than previous settlements.
"This shows that the economy is getting stable," said Marcio Bressan, a senior trader at Senso brokerage.

Analysts expect the bourse to show an uptrend after the settlements Monday with foreign investors resuming trade in Brazilian stocks. Besides telecom firms, others such as power and retail sector shares are expected to attract more investor interest, they added.
Among today's winners, traders cited Brazilian private bank BCN common shares, which soared 14.17 percent to 13.70 reais amid rumors that BBA Creditanstalt would acquire control of BCN, traders said.
The rumors were denied by BCN when they first arose last month.
Power firm Eletrobras preferred shares rose 1.8 percent to close at 339 reais.
Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred share rose 0.72 percent to end at 21 reais.
Petrobras preferred shares ended at 131.94 reais, off 1.52 percent.
